Power storage is reaching physical limits with current technology. Capacitors have to be used in order to release enough power quickly enough to work most directed energy applications. Batteries cannot deliver enough current without producing too much heat. The issue is that the plates within the cap can only get so close together before the voltage limit has to be reduced due to arcing between plates. Thus you can store a lot of power at low voltages, but as the voltage required scales, the caps get much larger, as the plates need more spacing.

You can increase the voltage by putting caps in series, but you halve the total capacitance while doubling the voltage when you put 2 in series. Therefore you need 4 caps (2 series in parallel) to double the voltage and keep the same capacitance.

The energy storage requirements can be met currently, but your uses would be limited, and the thing would look more like a ghostbusters pack than a handgun. Without a breakthrough in the storage of electricity, these are a ways off. until then, directed energy weapons will be vehicle mounted, or, at best crew served weapons.
